paper.title: Cost-Aware Multi-Objective Bandits: Theory and Application to Budgeted LLM Configuration Evaluation

settings.name_in_paper: Budgeted Online Configuration Selection (cost-aware multi-objective bandit, hypervolume-efficiency regret)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Multi-objective (vector-valued) rewards are out of scope of the ontology.
unmapped: vector-valued rewards in [0,1]^D with D objectives; performance scalarized via single-point hypervolume prod_j mu_i^(j)
random arm-dependent evaluation costs c_{i,t} in [lambda,1], i.i.d. per arm, unknown mean
regret measured in hypervolume per unit cost (efficiency gaps nu_star - nu_i)
the learner knows the cost lower bound lambda
settings.definition_quote: In online cost-aware configuration selection, the evaluation cost may be random. Specifically, evaluating configuration $i$ at round $t$ incurs a cost $c_{i,t}\in[\lambda,1], \quad \mu_i^c=\E[c_{i,t}]$ ... The hypervolume-efficiency regret under budget $B$ is $R_B^{\operatorname{HV}} = \sum_{t=1}^{T(B)}\Delta_{i_t}.$

settings.name_in_paper: Budgeted Pareto Configuration Identification (fixed-budget, deterministic known costs)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Multi-objective (vector-valued) rewards / Pareto set identification are out of scope of the ontology.
unmapped: vector-valued rewards in [0,1]^D; goal is to identify the Pareto set of non-dominated arms
deterministic arm-dependent costs c_i in [lambda,1], known to the learner
the learner knows the costs c_i and lambda
settings.definition_quote: For fixed-budget Pareto set identification, we instead consider deterministic and known evaluation costs, $c_i\in[\lambda,1].$ ... The learner adaptively evaluates configurations with deterministic costs $\{c_i\}_{i=1}^K$ and, upon exhausting the available budget, outputs an estimate $\widehat{\mathcal P}_B$. Its performance is measured by the misidentification probability

symbols.Delta_HV_i: hypervolume-efficiency gap nu_{i*} - nu_i, nu_i = H_i / mu_i^c

source.label: thm:cohv_ucb_regret
source.quote: Let $\alpha\ge 2$ and define $C_{\lambda,H}=\frac{4D}{\lambda}+\frac{4}{\lambda^2}.$ For each suboptimal arm $i\ne i^\star$, let $n_i(B)$ denote the number of times arm $i$ is pulled before the budget $B$ is exhausted. Then, under \textsc{CoHV-UCB}, $\mathbb E[n_i(B)] \le 1 + \lceil \frac{4\alpha C_{\lambda,H}^2\log T_B}{\Delta_i^2} \rceil + 2K(D+1)T_B^{2-2\alpha}.$

results.notes: Bound on expected number of pulls of a suboptimal arm i (per-arm).

conditions: lambda treated as a problem-dependent constant

source.label: thm:cohv_ucb_regret
source.quote: Consequently, the hypervolume-efficiency regret satisfies $\mathbb E[R_B^{\operatorname{HV}}] = \sum_{i\ne i^\star} \Delta_i\,\mathbb E[n_i(B)] = O\left(\sum_{i\ne i^\star} \frac{C_{\lambda,H}^2\log B}{\Delta_i}\right).$

results.notes: Hypervolume-efficiency regret: sum of efficiency gaps of pulled arms, in expectation (pseudo-regret form). Comparator is the best efficiency arm.

source.label: cor:standard_cohv_regret
source.quote: Under the conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:cohv_ucb_regret}, the standard budgeted hypervolume regret of \textsc{CoHV-UCB} satisfies $\mathbb E[R_B^{\operatorname{std}}] = O\left(\sum_{i\ne i^\star}\frac{C_{\lambda,H}^2\log B}{\Delta_i}\right).$

results.notes: Standard hypervolume regret against the optimal expected cumulative hypervolume under budget B (optimal budgeted policy). Proof uses an optional-sampling identity informally.

symbols.H_muc: cost-aware Pareto complexity max_{A nonempty} C(A)/gamma_(|A|)^2, C(A)=sum of costs, gamma ordered classification gaps

source.label: thm:copsi
source.quote: Let $K\ge 2$ and define $L_{K,\lambda}=1+\sum_{\ell=2}^{K}\frac{1}{1+(\ell-1)\lambda}.$ If the budget satisfies $B\ge 2L_{K,\lambda}H_{\boldsymbol\mu,c},$ then the Pareto set estimate returned by \textsc{CoPSI} satisfies $\Pr(\widehat{\mathcal P}_B\ne\mathcal P^\star)\le 2K^2D\exp(-\frac{B}{256L_{K,\lambda}H_{\boldsymbol\mu,c}}).$

results.notes: Probability marked high_probability as closest category for an error-probability bound.
